svg.title: Ship in gated slices
svg.desc: Proposed implementation sequence: agree compatibility, add records and public authoring, integrate shared readers and consumers, then prove the end-to-end workflow. Conflicting heads require deliberate reconciliation and old review pins remain intact.

g.text: TECHNICAL INVENTORY · PROPOSED DESIGN / 9
Ship in gated slices
Each gate needs its own tests and documentation before dependent work proceeds.
1 · FORMAT / READER GATE
Agree compatibility before writing
New reader keeps legacy history readable.
Old readers refuse unsupported format; no silent loss.
2 · RECORD / AUTHORING GATE
Add entities, revisions and selections
Public CLI, schema and validation together.
Implemented transition requires exact resolvable code.
4 · END-TO-END PROOF
Design → implement → review → reconcile
Verify subset coverage, retained plan and reverse uses.
Desktop + touch + offline + reload + conflict fixtures.
3 · SHARED CONSUMER GATE
One resolver, consistent readers
Queries + ERD directory + deck drawers.
Coverage and reconciliation retain the same provenance.
Competing heads stay competing. A saved pin remains readable, not automatically current.
Append a deliberate reconciliation; never choose a winner by timestamp or overwrite the proposal.
Existing reader rejects unknown inventory kinds. This needs an explicit compatibility boundary.
